rules: // Layer 2: a symlink in the tree can route a Normal-only path outside `base`. `exists()` is false
// for a dangling symlink, so the `is_symlink()` test is required, or the guard is skipped and the
// unvalidated join returned. `dunce::canonicalize` is required, or Windows `\\?\` UNC paths give
// false negatives. Containment compares whole components (`Path::starts_with`); a string-prefix
// check accepts a sibling like `<base>-evil`.
GRM-01.tags: why: symlink escape motivates Layer 2; guards kept: is_symlink test for dangling links, dunce canonicalize, component-wise starts_with (consequence made concrete); dropped: '(when exists OR is a symlink)' narration of the if.

rules: // Layer 2 catches a symlink routing a Normal-only path outside the root. `exists()` is false for
// a dangling symlink, so the symlink test is required, or the guard is skipped and the join
// returned unvalidated (a dangling symlink instead fails canonicalize with a safe `Io` error).
// `dunce::canonicalize` is required, or Windows `\\?\` UNC paths give false negatives.
// Containment compares whole components (`Path::starts_with`); a string-prefix check accepts a
// sibling like `<root>-evil`. The canonical path is returned so callers act on what was validated.
// The leaf is stat'ed once, before canonicalize, for both the branch and the carve-out below; a
// later stat (`Path::is_symlink()` is one) widens the TOCTOU window in the exploitable direction.
GRM-03.tags: why: Layer 2 purpose; guards kept (each own sentence): dangling-symlink is_symlink test + safe Io outcome, dunce canonicalize, component-wise starts_with, return canonical path, single leaf stat before canonicalize reused by carve-out; over 5-line cap because guards alone exceed it; dropped: narration of the if condition, 'we' phrasing.

rules: // The parent-directory fsync is required, or a crash can lose the rename.
// Unix-only: opening a directory as a `File` fails on Windows.
GRM-04.tags: guard: dir fsync for rename durability (fact + consequence); why: cfg(unix) because directory open fails on Windows; nothing dropped.

rules: /// Atomically replace the file `target` names, following a terminal symlink.
/// For user-authored files grim rewrites in place: [`atomic_write`]'s rename would
/// turn a symlinked one (a dotfiles-managed `grimoire.toml`, issue #117) into a
/// regular file and leave the managed copy stale. Grim-owned outputs keep plain
/// [`atomic_write`], which must clobber a planted link, or the link redirects the write.
/// # Errors
/// As [`atomic_write`].
GRM-05.tags: contract: summary, when to use (user-authored files), Errors section; guard: rename would replace a symlinked user file; guard: grim-owned outputs must not be unified onto this (planted link redirects write); pointer: issue #117 kept (resolves: grimoire-rs/grimoire#117); tightened to the 10-line app doc cap.

rules: // The sidecar is unlinked while the lock is still held: unlinked after the close, a waiter could
// lock the doomed inode past `try_acquire`'s identity re-check and run beside the next writer.
// Unix keeps the fd and lock until the close. On Windows (std opens with FILE_SHARE_DELETE) the
// name stays delete-pending until our handle closes; opens meanwhile get a permission error,
// which `try_acquire` must retry or fail spuriously. Best-effort: a leftover sidecar is harmless.
GRM-06.tags: guard: unlink-before-close ordering (consequence made concrete: two unserialized writers); why: Unix fd keeps lock alive; guard: Windows delete-pending window couples to try_acquire's PermissionDenied retry; why: best-effort remove; dropped: bullet layout, 'pre-cleanup status quo' provenance.

rules: // Write-then-rename in the same dir is required: load deletes an entry it cannot parse, so a
// concurrent load of a half-written file loses the good entry. The `.tmp` suffix keeps the
// in-flight file out of prune's `.json` filter. The tmp name is unique per write, not per repo:
// saves for one repo overlap (a panel open racing the card prefetch), and a shared path
// interleaves both into one file that the rename publishes torn. Racing saves last-write-win.
TS-03.tags: guards kept: write-then-rename in same dir (atomic rename), .tmp suffix vs prune's .json filter, per-write unique tmp name (provenance 'let both write' rewritten as present-tense guard); contract/why: racing saves last-write-win; dropped: 'each writes a whole entry now' provenance.

rules: // `path.resolve`, not `path.join`, is required: a relative PATH entry (`.`, `bin`,
// `./tools`) would give a relative path that the grim spawn resolves against its cwd,
// the workspace folder, so a repository shipping its own grim would win.
// Resolving before the access check keeps the probed file and the returned file the same.
TS-04.tags: guards kept: resolve-not-join (hijack by repo-shipped grim), resolve before access check (probe == return); dropped: the 'same threat as a bare grim' analogy (argument) and the `run()` pointer, which names no existing symbol (spawn lives in runJson).

rules: /** Basename of the ad-blocker-safe alias copy of a package root, written beside the package's
* own CAS directory: `p/<ns>/<pkg>/_root.json`. The site fetches the alias because a root URL
* ending in `<pkg>.json` fails to load in browsers running EasyList/EasyPrivacy when `<pkg>`
* matches one of their ~800 unanchored `/<word>.js` rules (`/hawkeye.js` blocks
* `/p/hawkeye/hawkeye.json`); no such rule matches a final `_root.json` segment.
* The leading `_` is required: `PACKAGE_RE` (`viewmodel/catalog.ts`) makes every package segment
* start with `[a-z0-9]`, so no package at any depth can collide with it. It must stay inside `p/`,
* or the `_headers` `/p/*` sandbox block no longer covers it. The canonical `p/<ns>/<pkg>.json` is
* still written; the alias is an extra copy for the site's fetch, never a wire-format change. */
TS-05.tags: contract: what the basename/path is; why+guard: alias exists because canonical <pkg>.json URLs are ad-blocked; provenance (2026-08-27 hawkeye incident, NetworkError) rewritten as a present-tense example; guards: _ prefix collision-proof via PACKAGE_RE (pointer resolves), must stay under p/ for _headers sandbox, canonical still written (no wire change).

rules: * Mount prefix for one source's mirrored wire tree: `""` for the `root: true` source and
* `/index/<label>` for every other source (`sources/mirror.ts`'s placement).
* Every wire URL written to `/data/catalog/catalog.json` must go through it: `/p/...` holds only
* the root source's copy, so an unprefixed non-root URL 404s silently and the catalog renders
* logo-less and README-less. `src/theme/utils/cas.ts` re-exports it for browser-side CAS URLs,
* so both halves of a build agree by construction; a second copy could drift.
* The live import is safe: `useImageIndex.ts` already pulls this module into the browser bundle.
TS-06.tags: contract: return values per source (pointer sources/mirror.ts resolves); guard: every emitted wire URL goes through it (past-tense 404 incident rewritten as present consequence); guard: theme re-exports rather than copies (pointer resolves); why: live import safe; dropped: LogoTile/IdentityBlock fallback detail, WIRE_ASSET_EXTENSIONS comparison (argument), __ocx.desc narrative.

rules: * Fetches the wire package root from the ad-blocker-safe alias
* `<wireBase>/p/<ns>/<pkg>/_root.json` (`sources/mirror.ts`), falling back on 404 to the
* byte-identical canonical `<wireBase>/p/<ns>/<pkg>.json`. `wireBase` is the source's mount
* prefix, `''` for the `root: true` source and `index/<label>` otherwise (see `wirePrefix`).
* Arguments accept refs/getters and refetch on change, post-mount only (SSR-safe); VitePress's
* router reuses the component across package navigations, so a one-shot `onMounted` fetch would
* leave stale data on screen. CAS asset URLs (`casUrl()`, `utils/cas.ts`) must be built from the
* bare `ns`/`pkg` given here; `root.name` carries the `ocx.sh/` prefix, so a URL from it 404s.
TS-07.tags: contract: fetch alias then canonical on 404, wireBase meaning, refs/getters refetch post-mount; guards: one-shot onMounted fetch leaves stale data under router reuse, CAS URLs from bare ns/pkg not root.name (404); pointers kept (mirror.ts, utils/cas.ts wirePrefix/casUrl resolve); dropped: schema root.schema.json aside, 'detail page reads it off frontmatter' narration, 'CAS gotcha' label.
